reviewStatus: ai-drafted: none of these items or passages has been human-reviewed; do not ship to students yet

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In paragraph 4, which detail best shows how Tomas feels after he falls and hears someone laugh?
choices: The weed snaps off at the top.
His face burns after the laughter.
He yanks at the weed a second time.
He tumbles backward into the dirt.
items.answer: His face burns after the laughter.
items.explanation: The text says that when someone laughed, Tomas felt his face burn, which signals embarrassment.

commonErrors.answer: He tumbles backward into the dirt.
commonErrors.why: This is what happens to him, not how he feels about it.

commonErrors.answer: He yanks at the weed a second time.
commonErrors.why: This shows his effort, not his reaction to the laughter.

commonErrors.answer: The weed snaps off at the top.
commonErrors.why: This is an earlier event that causes the fall, not a feeling.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which statement best expresses a theme of the story?
choices: Neighbors usually refuse to help people who are new in town.
Joining a community garden is the quickest way to make friends in a new town.
Patience and the right method can turn a frustrating job into a success.
Getting angry is a good way to push through a hard chore.
items.answer: Patience and the right method can turn a frustrating job into a success.
items.explanation: Tomas fails when he yanks angrily but succeeds once he follows Mrs. Okafor's advice to dig carefully, so the lesson is about patience and method.

commonErrors.answer: Joining a community garden is the quickest way to make friends in a new town.
commonErrors.why: Too narrow and unsupported; Tomas does not make friends quickly in the story.

commonErrors.answer: Neighbors usually refuse to help people who are new in town.
commonErrors.why: Reverses the story, in which Mrs. Okafor helps Tomas.

commonErrors.answer: Getting angry is a good way to push through a hard chore.
commonErrors.why: Contradicts the line that slow work beats angry work.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does Mrs. Okafor's offer of the trowel affect the events of the story?
choices: It explains why nobody has planted the plot for years.
It proves to Tomas that the other gardeners are laughing at him.
It convinces Tomas to ask for a different plot.
It gives Tomas a way to succeed, and his mood improves.
items.answer: It gives Tomas a way to succeed, and his mood improves.
items.explanation: After Tomas uses the trowel he lifts out a whole weed, grins, and finishes the day feeling better about being there.

commonErrors.answer: It convinces Tomas to ask for a different plot.
commonErrors.why: Tomas stays with the plot and clears part of it.

commonErrors.answer: It proves to Tomas that the other gardeners are laughing at him.
commonErrors.why: She helps him; the text does not say who laughed or connect it to her.

commonErrors.answer: It explains why nobody has planted the plot for years.
commonErrors.why: She says nobody has planted it but never gives a reason.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In paragraph 1, what does the phrase "like it had given up" suggest about the garden plot?
choices: It has been neglected for a long time.
Tomas has already decided to quit.
Someone broke the rake on purpose.
It is too small for anything useful to grow.
items.answer: It has been neglected for a long time.
items.explanation: A rusted rake slumped against the fence and weeds in every corner suggest a plot nobody has cared for in years.

commonErrors.answer: It is too small for anything useful to grow.
commonErrors.why: The text describes the plot as overgrown, not small.

commonErrors.answer: Tomas has already decided to quit.
commonErrors.why: The phrase describes the rake, and Tomas has only just arrived.

commonErrors.answer: Someone broke the rake on purpose.
commonErrors.why: Nothing suggests damage on purpose; the rake is merely rusted and leaning.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the sentence "So far it had only helped him meet dandelions" in paragraph 3 contribute to the story?
choices: It uses humor to show that the garden has not yet helped Tomas meet people.
It shows that Tomas has become an expert on plants.
It introduces dandelions as the main problem Tomas has to solve in the garden.
It explains why Tomas's family moved to town in August.
items.answer: It uses humor to show that the garden has not yet helped Tomas meet people.
items.explanation: The sentence follows his mother's hope that the garden would help him meet people and playfully shows that so far it has not.

commonErrors.answer: It introduces dandelions as the main problem Tomas has to solve in the garden.
commonErrors.why: The sentence is a joke; the weeds are not the central problem.

commonErrors.answer: It shows that Tomas has become an expert on plants.
commonErrors.why: Tomas is a beginner who struggles with a single weed.

commonErrors.answer: It explains why Tomas's family moved to town in August.
commonErrors.why: The move is mentioned earlier and has nothing to do with this joke.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which detail best supports the inference that the narrator's attitude toward Devon has softened by the end?
choices: She says working with him is the worst thing to happen this year.
She wanted to pour the water and be done quickly.
She measured the water even though she was annoyed.
She plans to ask if he wants to go first at practice.
items.answer: She plans to ask if he wants to go first at practice.
items.explanation: Offering Devon the first turn in the final lines shows respect that she did not feel when the entry began.

commonErrors.answer: She says working with him is the worst thing to happen this year.
commonErrors.why: This is her opinion at the start, before it changes.

commonErrors.answer: She wanted to pour the water and be done quickly.
commonErrors.why: This shows her impatience, not a softer attitude.

commonErrors.answer: She measured the water even though she was annoyed.
commonErrors.why: This shows she followed directions while still annoyed.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of the diary entry?
choices: A student wins the science fair by trusting her first guess.
A student discovers that expensive paper towels always soak up more water.
A student who is impatient with her partner's careful methods learns that his care leads to accurate results.
Two science fair partners argue so much about the project that one of them finally decides to quit the team.
items.answer: A student who is impatient with her partner's careful methods learns that his care leads to accurate results.
items.explanation: The narrator complains about Devon, then admits his fair test proved her guess wrong and decides being careful is not boring.

commonErrors.answer: Two science fair partners argue so much about the project that one of them finally decides to quit the team.
commonErrors.why: They never quit, and the narrator ends up grateful.

commonErrors.answer: A student discovers that expensive paper towels always soak up more water.
commonErrors.why: Reverses the result: the cheap brand won.

commonErrors.answer: A student wins the science fair by trusting her first guess.
commonErrors.why: Her guess was wrong, and no winner is mentioned.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the narrator change from the beginning of the entry to the end?
choices: She goes from annoyed by Devon to respecting his careful approach.
She goes from trusting her guess to disliking science.
She goes from excited about the fair to bored with it.
She goes from respecting Devon to feeling embarrassed whenever he is nearby.
items.answer: She goes from annoyed by Devon to respecting his careful approach.
items.explanation: She begins by calling Devon the worst partner and ends by admitting that being careful is not the same as being boring.

commonErrors.answer: She goes from trusting her guess to disliking science.
commonErrors.why: She never says she dislikes science.

commonErrors.answer: She goes from respecting Devon to feeling embarrassed whenever he is nearby.
commonErrors.why: Reverses her change.

commonErrors.answer: She goes from excited about the fair to bored with it.
commonErrors.why: Her interest in the fair is not what changes.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In the sentence "Devon didn't even gloat," what does the word "gloat" most nearly mean?
choices: apologize for the way he acted
laugh at a joke he had heard
complain loudly about a mistake he made
show off proudly about being right
items.answer: show off proudly about being right
items.explanation: Devon's test proved the narrator's guess wrong, yet he only wrote down numbers and said "Good thing we checked," so he did not boast.

commonErrors.answer: complain loudly about a mistake he made
commonErrors.why: Devon was not wrong, and he did not complain.

commonErrors.answer: apologize for the way he acted
commonErrors.why: He had nothing to apologize for in the text.

commonErrors.answer: laugh at a joke he had heard
commonErrors.why: The word describes how he reacts to being right, not a joke.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the first-person point of view shape what readers learn from the diary entry?
choices: Readers learn private feelings the narrator would never tell Devon.
Readers see the events through an outside narrator who judges both partners equally.
Readers learn what Devon is thinking while he sets up the paper towels.
Readers learn the final result of the science fair.
items.answer: Readers learn private feelings the narrator would never tell Devon.
items.explanation: Phrases such as "where nobody can read it" show the narrator sharing honest thoughts that stay hidden from Devon.

commonErrors.answer: Readers learn what Devon is thinking while he sets up the paper towels.
commonErrors.why: Only the narrator's thoughts are shown, not Devon's.

commonErrors.answer: Readers see the events through an outside narrator who judges both partners equally.
commonErrors.why: The narrator is one of the partners and clearly takes sides.

commonErrors.answer: Readers learn the final result of the science fair.
commonErrors.why: The entry ends before the fair takes place.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In paragraph 1, which detail best shows that Nia was avoiding the library?
choices: A sock was lying with the book under the bed.
The book was covered with dust.
The due date was seven weeks earlier.
She walked a longer way to school.
items.answer: She walked a longer way to school.
items.explanation: The text says she took a longer route so she would not pass the library doors, which is a deliberate way of staying away.

commonErrors.answer: The book was covered with dust.
commonErrors.why: This describes where the book had been, not Nia's behavior.

commonErrors.answer: A sock was lying with the book under the bed.
commonErrors.why: This is a detail about the book's hiding place.

commonErrors.answer: The due date was seven weeks earlier.
commonErrors.why: This is a fact about the lateness, not an action to avoid the library.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which statement best states the theme of this story?
choices: Careful planning prevents every kind of problem.
Facing a mistake can be easier than the worry of avoiding it.
Libraries should never charge fines for any late books returned.
Volunteering will always make people forgive a mistake.
items.answer: Facing a mistake can be easier than the worry of avoiding it.
items.explanation: Nia spent seven weeks dreading a problem that had disappeared on its own, and she feels better once she faces it.

commonErrors.answer: Libraries should never charge fines for any late books returned.
commonErrors.why: Too narrow; the story focuses on Nia's feelings.

commonErrors.answer: Volunteering will always make people forgive a mistake.
commonErrors.why: Nia does not need forgiveness; the fine had already been dropped.

commonErrors.answer: Careful planning prevents every kind of problem.
commonErrors.why: The story is about handling a problem, not preventing one.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: What problem does Nia face at the start of the story, and how is it resolved?
choices: She wants to keep the book and the librarian lets her.
She has an overdue book and fears the fine, but learns the fine was forgiven.
She loses a book and the librarian helps her find it.
She cannot afford a fine and earns the money by sorting the library's books.
items.answer: She has an overdue book and fears the fine, but learns the fine was forgiven.
items.explanation: Nia worries about an overdue book, and the librarian tells her fines under five dollars were forgiven.

commonErrors.answer: She loses a book and the librarian helps her find it.
commonErrors.why: She finds the book herself under her bed.

commonErrors.answer: She cannot afford a fine and earns the money by sorting the library's books.
commonErrors.why: She never pays; she owes nothing.

commonErrors.answer: She wants to keep the book and the librarian lets her.
commonErrors.why: She decides to return it.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does paragraph 2 contribute to the structure of the story?
choices: It shows the choices Nia weighs, which leads up to her decision.
It explains why the library charges fines and how much they cost.
It introduces the librarian as an important character.
It describes the layout of the library.
items.answer: It shows the choices Nia weighs, which leads up to her decision.
items.explanation: The paragraph lists three options Nia considers, setting up her choice to walk into the library.

commonErrors.answer: It explains why the library charges fines and how much they cost.
commonErrors.why: The library's rules are not explained.

commonErrors.answer: It introduces the librarian as an important character.
commonErrors.why: The librarian appears in the next paragraph.

commonErrors.answer: It describes the layout of the library.
commonErrors.why: No layout is described.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: From whose perspective is the story told, and how can you tell?
choices: The librarian's; the narrator explains why he smiles slowly at Nia's request.
Nia's; she tells the story using the word "I."
Nia's; the narrator shares her thoughts and worries but not the librarian's.
An all-knowing narrator who reveals every character's thoughts.
items.answer: Nia's; the narrator shares her thoughts and worries but not the librarian's.
items.explanation: The narrator uses "she" yet reveals only Nia's reasoning and feelings, such as dreading the problem for seven weeks.

commonErrors.answer: The librarian's; the narrator explains why he smiles slowly at Nia's request.
commonErrors.why: We never learn what the librarian thinks.

commonErrors.answer: Nia's; she tells the story using the word "I."
commonErrors.why: The narrator uses "she," so it is third person.

commonErrors.answer: An all-knowing narrator who reveals every character's thoughts.
commonErrors.why: Only Nia's thoughts are revealed.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which line from the poem best supports the idea that the speaker is anxious about the test?
choices: and slides a folded note across the seat:
its yellow side still damp with dawn.
and the words slip off and hide.
The driver nods, and I nod back,
items.answer: and the words slip off and hide.
items.explanation: The words disappearing from the speaker's memory show worry about forgetting the facts.

commonErrors.answer: its yellow side still damp with dawn.
commonErrors.why: This describes the bus, not the speaker's worry.

commonErrors.answer: The driver nods, and I nod back,
commonErrors.why: This is a friendly gesture, not a worry.

commonErrors.answer: and slides a folded note across the seat:
commonErrors.why: This is the kind act that comes later.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which statement best expresses a theme of this poem?
choices: Studying hard is the only way to feel ready for a test.
A small act of kindness can ease someone's worries.
Riding the bus is more fun than walking to school.
Mornings are the hardest part of the school day.
items.answer: A small act of kindness can ease someone's worries.
items.explanation: The speaker's mood lifts after Jada's note, shown by the stones losing their weight in the last stanza.

commonErrors.answer: Studying hard is the only way to feel ready for a test.
commonErrors.why: Studying is not what changes the speaker's mood.

commonErrors.answer: Mornings are the hardest part of the school day.
commonErrors.why: The poem is more about worry and friendship than mornings.

commonErrors.answer: Riding the bus is more fun than walking to school.
commonErrors.why: Walking is never mentioned.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the speaker's mood change from the second stanza to the fourth stanza?
choices: from excited to disappointed
from worried to cheerful
from calm to frightened
from lonely to embarrassed
items.answer: from worried to cheerful
items.explanation: The second stanza has the words hiding and a flipping stomach, while the fourth ends with the speaker smiling and ready.

commonErrors.answer: from excited to disappointed
commonErrors.why: Reverses the change.

commonErrors.answer: from lonely to embarrassed
commonErrors.why: The speaker is worried, not lonely, and ends smiling.

commonErrors.answer: from calm to frightened
commonErrors.why: The speaker starts out nervous, not calm.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In the first stanza, what does the phrase "heavy as a sack of stones" suggest about the speaker?
choices: The speaker feels weighed down by worry as well as by the load.
The speaker is too weak to climb the steps.
The speaker likes carrying heavy things.
The speaker's backpack is actually filled with large, heavy rocks.
items.answer: The speaker feels weighed down by worry as well as by the load.
items.explanation: In the last stanza the stones lose their weight after the note arrives, so the heaviness stands for the speaker's worry.

commonErrors.answer: The speaker's backpack is actually filled with large, heavy rocks.
commonErrors.why: It is a comparison, not literal stones.

commonErrors.answer: The speaker likes carrying heavy things.
commonErrors.why: Nothing suggests enjoyment.

commonErrors.answer: The speaker is too weak to climb the steps.
commonErrors.why: The speaker does climb the steps.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the third stanza change the direction of the poem?
choices: It introduces a new speaker who tells a different story.
It shows the speaker deciding to skip the test.
It repeats the description of the bus and driver from the first stanza.
It introduces an event that starts to lift the speaker's worry.
items.answer: It introduces an event that starts to lift the speaker's worry.
items.explanation: Until the third stanza the mood is nervous; Jada's note is the turning point that leads to the cheerful ending.

commonErrors.answer: It repeats the description of the bus and driver from the first stanza.
commonErrors.why: Jada's note is new.

commonErrors.answer: It introduces a new speaker who tells a different story.
commonErrors.why: The speaker stays the same.

commonErrors.answer: It shows the speaker deciding to skip the test.
commonErrors.why: The speaker never mentions skipping the test.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: According to paragraph 3, what does a longer waggle tell the other bees?
choices: The flowers are in a different direction.
The flowers are farther from the hive.
The flowers contain more nectar.
The flowers are closer to the sun.
items.answer: The flowers are farther from the hive.
items.explanation: The paragraph states that the length of the waggle shows the distance, with a longer waggle meaning farther away.

commonErrors.answer: The flowers are in a different direction.
commonErrors.why: Direction is shown by the angle, not the length.

commonErrors.answer: The flowers contain more nectar.
commonErrors.why: The passage never links length to nectar.

commonErrors.answer: The flowers are closer to the sun.
commonErrors.why: Position relative to the sun is shown by the angle.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the whole passage?
choices: A single leader bee gives orders that every other bee in the colony must follow.
Honeybees dance mainly to celebrate finding flowers.
Scientists have invented many ways to talk to insects.
Honeybees use a dance to share where food is, which helps the whole colony.
items.answer: Honeybees use a dance to share where food is, which helps the whole colony.
items.explanation: The passage explains the waggle dance and ends by saying a group can do more by sharing information.

commonErrors.answer: A single leader bee gives orders that every other bee in the colony must follow.
commonErrors.why: The first paragraph says no single bee is in charge.

commonErrors.answer: Scientists have invented many ways to talk to insects.
commonErrors.why: Scientists only test the dance; they do not talk to bees.

commonErrors.answer: Honeybees dance mainly to celebrate finding flowers.
commonErrors.why: The dance carries information, not celebration.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the author explain the waggle dance in paragraphs 2 and 3?
choices: First describing scientists' tests, then describing what the bee does.
First describing what the bee does, then explaining what the movements mean.
By comparing the dance to the way that people give each other directions to a place.
By giving reasons that bees prefer certain flowers.
items.answer: First describing what the bee does, then explaining what the movements mean.
items.explanation: Paragraph 2 describes the bee's actions and paragraph 3 explains that angle shows direction and length shows distance.

commonErrors.answer: First describing scientists' tests, then describing what the bee does.
commonErrors.why: The tests come in paragraph 4.

commonErrors.answer: By comparing the dance to the way that people give each other directions to a place.
commonErrors.why: No comparison to people is made.

commonErrors.answer: By giving reasons that bees prefer certain flowers.
commonErrors.why: Flower choice is not explained.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In paragraph 2, what does the word "forager" most likely mean?
choices: a young bee that has just hatched
a bee that guards the hive
a bee that builds the honeycomb
a bee that searches for food
items.answer: a bee that searches for food
items.explanation: The forager discovers flowers rich in nectar and flies back, so the word refers to a food-finder.

commonErrors.answer: a bee that guards the hive
commonErrors.why: Guarding is not described, and she flies off to find flowers.

commonErrors.answer: a bee that builds the honeycomb
commonErrors.why: She dances on the honeycomb but is not building it.

commonErrors.answer: a young bee that has just hatched
commonErrors.why: Nothing suggests age.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: What is the main purpose of paragraph 4 in the passage?
choices: It explains in detail how honeybees slowly evolved over many years to dance.
It argues that the dance is rarely used.
It shows how other bees use the message and how scientists checked the system.
It introduces a problem that the dance cannot solve.
items.answer: It shows how other bees use the message and how scientists checked the system.
items.explanation: The paragraph describes bees following the dance and then scientists testing it by moving food.

commonErrors.answer: It introduces a problem that the dance cannot solve.
commonErrors.why: No problem with the dance is described.

commonErrors.answer: It explains in detail how honeybees slowly evolved over many years to dance.
commonErrors.why: Evolution is not discussed.

commonErrors.answer: It argues that the dance is rarely used.
commonErrors.why: The passage presents the dance as a major method.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: According to paragraph 2, how does a barnacle survive when the tide goes out?
choices: It slows water loss with tough skin.
It shuts its shell plates to keep a bit of seawater inside.
It ties itself to neighbors with silky threads.
It slides into a shady crack in the rocks to wait for the waves.
items.answer: It shuts its shell plates to keep a bit of seawater inside.
items.explanation: The paragraph says the barnacle closes its shell and traps a drop of seawater to stay moist.

commonErrors.answer: It slides into a shady crack in the rocks to wait for the waves.
commonErrors.why: This is a sea star strategy in paragraph 3.

commonErrors.answer: It ties itself to neighbors with silky threads.
commonErrors.why: This is how mussels hold on.

commonErrors.answer: It slows water loss with tough skin.
commonErrors.why: This is a sea star feature.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which statement states the central idea of this passage?
choices: Waves are the most dangerous threat to all ocean life.
Intertidal animals have different ways of surviving a harsh home.
Barnacles are the strongest animals living on any rocky seashore in the world.
Low tide is the safest time to visit a tide pool.
items.answer: Intertidal animals have different ways of surviving a harsh home.
items.explanation: Paragraphs 2 through 4 each show a different animal solving problems of waves, sun, and dryness.

commonErrors.answer: Barnacles are the strongest animals living on any rocky seashore in the world.
commonErrors.why: Barnacles are only one example.

commonErrors.answer: Low tide is the safest time to visit a tide pool.
commonErrors.why: Safety is not the main focus.

commonErrors.answer: Waves are the most dangerous threat to all ocean life.
commonErrors.why: The passage describes several challenges, not just waves.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the author develop the main idea in paragraphs 2 through 4?
choices: By telling a story about a visit to the shore.
By comparing the three animals to decide which one is the strongest overall.
By explaining why the tide moves in and out.
By describing a different animal and its way of surviving in each paragraph.
items.answer: By describing a different animal and its way of surviving in each paragraph.
items.explanation: Barnacles, sea stars, and mussels each get a paragraph, with details about how they cope.

commonErrors.answer: By comparing the three animals to decide which one is the strongest overall.
commonErrors.why: No ranking occurs.

commonErrors.answer: By telling a story about a visit to the shore.
commonErrors.why: The text is explanatory, not a personal story.

commonErrors.answer: By explaining why the tide moves in and out.
commonErrors.why: The tides are not explained.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In paragraph 2, what does the word "reserve" mean in the phrase "That tiny reserve keeps the barnacle moist"?
choices: an area set aside to protect wildlife
a quiet, shy manner
a supply saved for later
a request to hold a seat
items.answer: a supply saved for later
items.explanation: The drop of seawater is stored inside the shell and used until the tide returns.

commonErrors.answer: an area set aside to protect wildlife
commonErrors.why: Real meaning of the word, but it does not fit a drop of water.

commonErrors.answer: a quiet, shy manner
commonErrors.why: A different meaning that does not fit the sentence.

commonErrors.answer: a request to hold a seat
commonErrors.why: A different meaning that does not fit the sentence.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: What is the author's main purpose in paragraph 5?
choices: to warn readers that tide pool animals can be dangerous to touch
to warn readers that tide pool animals are dangerous
to encourage readers to treat tide pool animals with care
to convince readers to avoid the shore
items.answer: to encourage readers to treat tide pool animals with care
items.explanation: The author recommends stepping carefully and touching gently, and says the animals deserve respect.

commonErrors.answer: to warn readers that tide pool animals are dangerous
commonErrors.why: The advice is to be gentle with the animals.

commonErrors.answer: to warn readers that tide pool animals can be dangerous to touch
commonErrors.why: Tides are not explained.

commonErrors.answer: to convince readers to avoid the shore
commonErrors.why: The author encourages visiting, with care.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: According to paragraph 2, why does the Moon shine?
choices: Sunlight passes through it from behind.
It makes its own light, much like a lamp does.
Earth's shadow makes it glow.
Its surface reflects light from the Sun.
items.answer: Its surface reflects light from the Sun.
items.explanation: The paragraph compares the Moon to a mirror that bounces light.

commonErrors.answer: It makes its own light, much like a lamp does.
commonErrors.why: The paragraph says it makes no light of its own.

commonErrors.answer: Earth's shadow makes it glow.
commonErrors.why: The shadow is not the source of light.

commonErrors.answer: Sunlight passes through it from behind.
commonErrors.why: The light is reflected, not passed through.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: What is the central idea of this passage?
choices: The Moon's phases occur because we see different amounts of its lit half as it orbits Earth.
The Moon produces more light at some times than at others.
The Moon changes its real shape during each trip around Earth.
Earth's shadow slowly covers a little more of the Moon each night and then uncovers it again.
items.answer: The Moon's phases occur because we see different amounts of its lit half as it orbits Earth.
items.explanation: The passage explains that half the Moon is always lit and our viewing angle changes during its orbit.

commonErrors.answer: Earth's shadow slowly covers a little more of the Moon each night and then uncovers it again.
commonErrors.why: This is the belief the author corrects.

commonErrors.answer: The Moon changes its real shape during each trip around Earth.
commonErrors.why: The Moon does not change shape.

commonErrors.answer: The Moon produces more light at some times than at others.
commonErrors.why: It produces none of its own.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the author respond to the common belief introduced in paragraph 1?
choices: By correcting it, first explaining the real cause and later showing when Earth's shadow does matter.
By agreeing with the belief and then adding several small details about how the Moon moves in space.
By ignoring it and writing only about eclipses.
By listing scientists who disagree about the cause.
items.answer: By correcting it, first explaining the real cause and later showing when Earth's shadow does matter.
items.explanation: Paragraphs 2-4 give the actual cause of phases, and paragraph 5 says Earth's shadow causes only eclipses.

commonErrors.answer: By agreeing with the belief and then adding several small details about how the Moon moves in space.
commonErrors.why: The author says the real explanation is different.

commonErrors.answer: By ignoring it and writing only about eclipses.
commonErrors.why: The belief is addressed directly and eclipses appear only at the end.

commonErrors.answer: By listing scientists who disagree about the cause.
commonErrors.why: No scientists are named or listed.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: In paragraph 4, what does the word "waning" mean?
choices: growing larger
turning dark suddenly
staying the same
growing smaller
items.answer: growing smaller
items.explanation: The paragraph says the visible shape shrinks, which is called waning, back toward new moon.

commonErrors.answer: growing larger
commonErrors.why: That is waxing.

commonErrors.answer: staying the same
commonErrors.why: The shape changes.

commonErrors.answer: turning dark suddenly
commonErrors.why: The change is gradual.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does paragraph 2 fit into the structure of the passage?
choices: It describes how lunar eclipses happen.
It gives a basic fact about the Moon's light that the later explanation depends on.
It summarizes the whole passage.
It gives a counterexample that disproves the explanation given later in paragraph 3.
items.answer: It gives a basic fact about the Moon's light that the later explanation depends on.
items.explanation: Knowing that the Moon reflects sunlight and that half is lit is needed to understand the phases in paragraph 3.

commonErrors.answer: It gives a counterexample that disproves the explanation given later in paragraph 3.
commonErrors.why: It supports paragraph 3.

commonErrors.answer: It summarizes the whole passage.
commonErrors.why: It introduces only one fact.

commonErrors.answer: It describes how lunar eclipses happen.
commonErrors.why: Eclipses appear in the last paragraph.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to a student who cannot print at home?
choices: The student must hand in written work or skip the assignment.
The student can use a printer in any classroom.
The student is sent to the principal's office.
The student is given several extra days to finish the work at home.
items.answer: The student must hand in written work or skip the assignment.
items.explanation: Paragraph 3 says such a student must hand in written work or skip the assignment.

commonErrors.answer: The student is given several extra days to finish the work at home.

commonErrors.answer: The student can use a printer in any classroom.
commonErrors.why: Printers are said to be in the library.

commonErrors.answer: The student is sent to the principal's office.
commonErrors.why: Nothing in the passage describes a punishment.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: How does the paragraph that begins "Some people say" fit into the argument?
choices: It changes the author's claim.
It introduces a new reason supported by a survey.
It restates the author's reasons in a summary.
It raises an objection and answers it.

commonErrors.answer: It restates the author's reasons in a summary.
commonErrors.why: The summary comes in the final paragraph.

commonErrors.answer: It changes the author's claim.
commonErrors.why: The claim stays the same.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: What is the author's main purpose in writing the passage?
choices: to inform readers about the history of school libraries
to entertain readers with a story about homework
to persuade readers that library hours should be extended
to describe what students usually do in the library each school day

commonErrors.answer: to entertain readers with a story about homework

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which reason is best supported by evidence in the passage?

Students would prefer to stay at school.
items.answer: Students need a quiet place to work, as shown by the student council survey.

commonErrors.answer: An open library would raise test scores across the entire school.

commonErrors.answer: Spending time in libraries makes students better at every subject.

commonErrors.answer: Students would prefer to stay at school.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Why is the third reason weaker than the first two?
choices: It is about a different topic than the one stated in the author's main claim.
It relies on a survey with too few students.
It contradicts the author's second reason.
It states a broad claim as if it were common knowledge, without evidence.
items.answer: It states a broad claim as if it were common knowledge, without evidence.
items.explanation: The phrase "Everyone knows" replaces proof, while the first two reasons give a survey and concrete facts.

commonErrors.answer: It is about a different topic than the one stated in the author's main claim.

commonErrors.answer: It relies on a survey with too few students.

commonErrors.answer: It contradicts the author's second reason.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Read the sentence: "The hikers were famished after climbing all day, so they devoured the sandwiches in minutes." What does "famished" mean?
choices: very proud
extremely tired
very hungry
very cold
items.answer: very hungry
items.explanation: Devouring food quickly is a clue that they were extremely hungry.

commonErrors.answer: extremely tired
commonErrors.why: Plausible after a hike, but eating quickly points to hunger.

commonErrors.answer: very cold
commonErrors.why: Nothing mentions weather.

commonErrors.answer: very proud

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Read the sentence: "Mina's brother was unreliable; he often promised to help and then forgot." Using the word parts, what does "unreliable" mean?
choices: usually easy to forget about
always willing to help
not able to be depended on
completely dishonest
items.answer: not able to be depended on

commonErrors.answer: usually easy to forget about
commonErrors.why: Confuses the result with the meaning.

commonErrors.answer: always willing to help
commonErrors.why: Ignores the prefix un-.

commonErrors.answer: completely dishonest
commonErrors.why: He forgot, but the sentence does not say he lies.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: The root "port" means "carry" and the prefix "trans-" means "across." What does the word "transport" most likely mean?
choices: to hold something firmly in one place
to carry from one place to another
to carry only upward
to store many things
items.answer: to carry from one place to another
items.explanation: Trans- (across) plus port (carry) means carrying across.

commonErrors.answer: to hold something firmly in one place
commonErrors.why: Opposite of moving across.

commonErrors.answer: to carry only upward
commonErrors.why: Across does not mean upward.

commonErrors.answer: to store many things
commonErrors.why: Storing does not involve moving across.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Read the sentence: "The bank of the river was slippery after the rain." Which meaning of "bank" is used?
choices: the sloping land beside a river
to tilt to one side
a business where people keep money
a row of switches or lights
items.answer: the sloping land beside a river

commonErrors.answer: a business where people keep money
commonErrors.why: Common meaning, but it does not fit a river.

commonErrors.answer: a row of switches or lights
commonErrors.why: Does not fit.

commonErrors.answer: to tilt to one side
commonErrors.why: Verb meaning that does not fit.

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: The suffix "-ology" means "the study of" and "bio-" means "life." What does "biology" most likely mean?

the study of stars and planets
the study of rocks and minerals
the study of living things
items.answer: the study of living things

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Read the sentence: "The teacher's stern look made the whole class fall silent." What does "stern" mean here?

confused and puzzled
serious and strict
the back end of a boat

commonErrors.answer: confused and puzzled

commonErrors.answer: the back end of a boat

commonErrors.answer: hidden

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Read the sentence: "Unlike her outgoing sister, Lena was reserved; she rarely spoke in large groups." What does "reserved" mean?

quiet and keeping thoughts private
saved for someone else

items.subject: ela
items.prompt: Which sentence contains a simile?

commonErrors.answer: The classroom was a zoo.
